text.p: The following are the main stories from Tuesday morning's Albanian newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- An International Monetary Fund four-member mission is in Albania to assess the economic situation and suspected pyramid schemes.
- Three main opposition parties say they would like a new constitution to be passed by a Constitutional Assembly and later submitted to a popular referendum.
- The Supreme Court has turned down a bail request from the son-in-law of late communist dictator Enver Hoxha. Klement Kolaneci faces charges of "participation in armed bands".

- Ruling Democratic Party MP Azem Hajdari and the Independent Trade Unions head Valer Xheka have taken each other to court. Hajdari accuses Xheka of corruption whereas Xheka charged Hajdari slandered him.
- Police have turned down a request from Azem Hajdari, the self-proclaimed leader of the Independent Trade Unions, to stage a peaceful rally on the main boulevard.
- Police have arrested a man suspected of being one of the authors of a spectacular bank robbery which netted $306,000.
- Albanians started taking the second dose of a vaccine to prevent polio. The World Health Organisation has promised Albania that member states will take care of vaccinating of Albanian immigrants.
- Albania's Consumer Price Index rose by 1.6 percent in October due to the higher prices of tomatoes and cucumbers.
- Albanian police have arrested about 100 Kurds who reached the Albanian coast in speedboats and were destined to reach Italy across the Adriatic sea.
- Albania and Poland promised each other mutual support in their bids to join European forums during the visit to Albania of Polish Finance Minister Grzegorz Kolodko.
